title: Tear-off
description: A roll of paper ticket stubs printed with recently played songs, on clean fine stock with crisp ink and perforations that feather slightly as they tear. Twist the end one and it lifts and unzips hole by hole; yank it and it snaps clean. Drag a torn stub to the reader along the bottom and it pulls itself square into the slot, feeds in and plays that song's preview with a rolling clock; drop in another and the first is pushed back out.
intent: One physical mechanic finished to the edge: a perforation that unzips bridge by bridge under your own twist and snaps under a yank, and a reader that takes the stub you tore and plays its song.

changelog.summary:
Paper fibre texture: a tileable 256px stock generated once on a canvas (cloudy formation, dark pulp fibres, light fibres, a few long strands, pulp specks) fills every ticket and the roll through four offset/rotated pattern variants.
Print grain: a second tooth layer over the printed face adds paper ridges and tiny ink voids, so ink, cover and barcode read as printed into the stock.
Ink sits in the paper: the face multiplies onto the paper, text gets a 0.6px ink bleed, covers print slightly flatter (saturate 0.9, contrast 0.95), and barcode bars are roughened by a fibre displacement filter with a soft edge.
Misregistration: each ticket carries a seeded 0.25-0.65px offset for a spot plate taken from its cover colour, ghosting behind the type and as a sliver beside the cover.
Frayed perforation holes: each half-hole is a seeded ragged ellipse that still stretches into an oval under load, with paper whiskers reaching into the hole.
Torn edges show fibres: broken bridges leave a ragged seven-point nub, a light exposed-core band, a fine dark edge line and four fibre whiskers instead of the heavy ink outline.
Contact shadow: a 0.7px soft shadow under every ticket's real outline seats the paper on the table, visible along the bottom edge and through the holes.
Lift shadow and curl: the ticket you twist lifts with perforation strain and torn fraction, casting a blurred offset shadow and tilting up to 7 degrees about the seam with a crease-to-highlight shading band; a partly torn end keeps a small resting curl.
Stubs float: a held stub lifts with shadow and a 2.2% scale (replacing the CSS scale), and thrown stubs cast a speed-scaled shadow that settles as they land; tilt is skipped under reduced motion.
Grain painted at device resolution (devicePixelRatio, capped at 2) and shown at 256 units, so fibres, specks and ink voids stay crisp hairs on Retina instead of soft smudges.
Stronger stock: formation raised to cloud*0.4, dark fibres to 0.08-0.2 alpha, long strands and light fibres lifted, pulp specks drawn as tiny crisp ellipses.
Every ticket gets its own seeded paper and tooth pattern (offset plus a quarter-turn or mirror), all pointing at one decoded image, so no two stubs share the same specks.
Grain is painted in an idle callback so the mount and first frame are no longer blocked.
Frayed holes where they can be seen: holes beside loaded or broken bridges fray up to 0.35 with 1-2px whiskers at 0.6px; intact seams draw a cheap elliptical arc.
Tilt only while held: the perspective rotation eases in on grab and back to flat on release, so the resting end ticket stays crisp; its resting curl now shows as visible shading.
Fixed the entrance and exit scaling from the left edge: the body scales about its centre again and leave() clears the inline origin.
Perf: the lift shadow is its own layer, the body is promoted only while lifting or held, and each ticket's outline is one path reused by fill, texture, tooth, curl, contact and shadow, so a dirty frame writes one d instead of six.
Roll matches the stubs: 1px outline at 30% ink, softer spin lines, and a multi-stop eased cylinder shading with a highlight about 35% across.

Paper formation (cloudy mottling) cut to a quarter: depth 0.4 -> 0.1, light side 1.6x -> 1.2x, per-pixel noise 0.06 -> 0.016; mottling falls from 6.8 to 1.4 luminance levels of spread, worst blotch from 34 to 7.
Pulp tone neutralised from brown rgb(92 78 60) to warm grey rgb(112 106 98), so nothing reads as a stain.
Dark fibres 760 at 0.08-0.2 alpha, 3-14px, 0.3-0.75px wide -> 220 at 0.04-0.08 alpha, 3-10px, 0.25-0.5px wide.
Light fibres 300 at 0.26-0.58 alpha -> 140 at 0.1-0.2 alpha, 0.4-0.8px wide.
Long strands 26 at 0.08-0.16 alpha -> 8 at 0.03-0.05 alpha, 18-36px.
Pulp specks removed (80 dark dots at 0.3-0.6 alpha -> none).
Print tooth over the ink: white ink voids removed (0.9% of pixels at 31-71% alpha -> none), ridge sheen onset 0.2 -> 0.25 and peak alpha 28% -> 9%, dark pits 1.6% at 9-18% alpha -> 0.4% at 3-6% alpha.
Misregistration removed: the 0.25-0.65px spot-colour ghost behind the type and the sliver beside the cover are gone (--to-mx/--to-my dropped).
Ink bleed on type 0.6px at 50% -> 0.3px at 20%.
Barcode ink: fibre displacement removed (feTurbulence + displacement 0.9 -> none), softness blur 0.18 -> 0.12, bars print straight.
Covers print true: saturate 0.9 + contrast 0.95 -> saturate 0.97 only.
Perforation fray: hole raggedness 0.35 -> 0.1, hole whiskers 2 at 1-2px -> 1 at 0.4-0.8px.
Torn nubs calmer: length 2.6 -> 2.4, reach variance 0.5-1.6x -> 0.75-1.15x, drift 0.09 -> 0.04, whiskers 4 at 0.8-2.8px -> 2 at 0.5-1.3px with a narrower spread.
Torn edge line 46% ink at 0.7px -> 26% at 0.6px; exposed core band 1.8px -> 1.2px and paler; fibre strokes 30% ink at 0.6px -> 16% at 0.4px.
Contact shadow opacity 0.16 -> 0.08, blur 0.7 -> 0.6, offset (0.35, 0.9) -> (0.25, 0.6).
Lift shadow opacity 0.2 -> 0.12, offset (3, 9) -> (2, 6)px, blur 7 -> 8, grow 3% -> 2%.
Curl tilt 7deg -> 3.5deg; curl shading stops halved (edge 0.16 -> 0.07 ink, highlight 0.18 -> 0.08 white) and eased linearly instead of square-root; resting curl 0.3 -> 0.2.

Reader along the bottom: a slim flat player centred under the roll (440px on desktop, full width less 16px gutters on phone) with a dark slot in its top edge sized to the ticket (ticket width + 12px).
Magnetic slot: inside an ellipse of 0.75 ticket widths by 1.3 ticket heights the held stub's hand is pulled toward the docked pose (up to 94%) and the stub turns square; the pull fades in over the first 28px of travel so grabbing a stub near the reader never jumps, and the slot turns accent and opens 1.5x when letting go would insert.
Insert animation: the stub seats square on the mouth, the rollers catch it (12% of its height in 120ms with a low clunk), hold 70ms, then draw it in over 540ms ease-in-out under a soft roller hiss; the stub is clipped at the slot line so it slides under the player's edge.
Tear and carry in one gesture: yank the end ticket off and keep dragging it straight into the slot; reach is measured from both the hand and the stub centre so a stub swinging from its corner still catches.
Tap a stub, or focus it and press Enter, to have it carried to the reader and fed in.
Now playing: cover, title, artist and a rolling 0:00 / 0:30 clock in tabular odometer digits, a 2px progress line written per frame outside React, a morphing play/pause and an eject button.
Audio starts only from the insert gesture: a silent clip unlocks one shared audio element on the first touch, the preview URL is prefetched when a stub is torn or grabbed and buffered during the draw, and the song fades in once the ticket is fully inside.
States: loading runs a travelling multi-stop shimmer on the progress line, no confident match shows No preview with play disabled, a failed direct URL falls back to the same-origin stream, blocked autoplay lands on paused so one tap plays it, and the empty reader reads Nothing playing / Drop a ticket in the slot.
Swap: inserting another ticket pushes the one inside back out in 440ms while the new stub waits just above the mouth, then catches as soon as the mouth is clear; the old song fades out over 240ms.
Eject: the stub is pushed out over 640ms (ease-out cubic) and nudged onto the table with a gentle sideways drift and about 9 degrees of turn; ejecting mid-draw reverses it, ejecting before the rollers catch sets it back down, and an ejected stub can be inserted again.
Tearing no longer auto-plays the stub and the purple barcode progress on stubs is gone; the reader is the only place a song plays.
Table floor moved up to the slot line so stubs rest above the player, desktop piles sit right of the slot, the held stub is clamped to the floor so letting go over the player never launches it, and resizes clamp stubs instead of waking them.
Count, sound and New roll moved from the bottom-left to under the title so the bottom belongs to the reader; the roll's minimum height moved down 24px on desktop and 8px on phone to clear them.
Sound toggle mutes the preview instead of stopping it; New roll and resizes keep the song in the reader playing (an insert in flight completes at once).
Body capacity 16 -> 20 so a stub feeding and one ejecting fit beside a full roll and pile.
